claims.text: Conventionally processed NbMoTaW-based refractory HEAs have a coarse-grained microstructure.
Conventionally processed NbMoTaW-based refractory HEAs have limited twin-boundary density.
Room-temperature cold deformation followed by annealing at 800–900 °C will induce a nanotwinned microstructure in NbMoTaW-based refractory HEAs.
Annealing at 800–900 °C will stabilize the induced nanotwinned microstructure.
The proposed processing will produce a refined BCC microstructure.
The proposed processing will produce a high density of coherent twin boundaries.
The induced twin boundaries will impede dislocation motion.
Impeded dislocation motion at the twin boundaries will enhance strength.
The induced twin boundaries will enhance ductility.
The induced twin boundaries will act as sinks for irradiation-induced defects.
Defect absorption at twin boundaries will promote irradiation-defect annihilation or recovery.
Optimized processing will keep the twin boundaries stable during prolonged high-temperature exposure.
Optimized processing will keep the twin boundaries stable during prolonged irradiation exposure.
The nanotwinned alloy will have higher yield strength than a conventionally processed NbMoTaW-based alloy.
The nanotwinned alloy will have greater ductility than a conventionally processed NbMoTaW-based alloy.
The nanotwinned alloy will exhibit enhanced irradiation-defect recovery under high-temperature service conditions.
The proposed intervention will maintain thermal stability at approximately 1000 °C.
The proposed intervention will maintain stability under irradiation.
Excessive twin coarsening or instability during service could eliminate the anticipated benefits.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis and mechanism state that processing will maintain or ensure twin-boundary stability during high-temperature irradiation, whereas the uncertainty field says that long-term thermal and irradiation stability remains unknown and that the boundaries may coarsen or degrade.
